properties.foundation_analysis: Subterranean foundation consists of Early Carboniferous sedimentary bedrock interbedded with volcanic basalt and dolerite intrusions of the Midland Valley basin. Superstructure lithics are predominantly local Craigleith and Hailes sandstone, characterized by fine-to-medium grained quartz arenite bound with silica and minor iron oxides, yielding high compressive strength and buff-grey coloration. Historic bedding joints utilize hot-mixed non-hydraulic slaked lime and coarse volcanic sand mortars. Subsurface drainage directs into modified urban culverts overlying glacial till.

properties.primary_surfacing: Engineered roadway and paved pedestrian curbs
properties.wear_characteristics: Authentic environmental patina and drainage grading

properties.botanical_analysis: Mature urban parkland specimens dispersed across the garden perimeter: *Platanus × acerifolia* (London plane), *Acer pseudoplatanus* (sycamore), and *Tilia × europaea* (common lime). Late September phenology (2026-09-23): Dense canopies showing early autumn senescence, leaf margins exhibiting pale chlorosis, yellow-ochre tipping on lime and sycamore branches, minimal canopy thinning, and sparse early leaf scatter on turf beneath drip lines.

properties.architectural_summary: Central civic focal point is West Register House (formerly St George's Church, 1811–1814, designed by Robert Reid after Robert Adam), featuring a monumental Neoclassical temple front with an Ionic portico, dentiled pediment, elevated cylindrical drum surrounded by paired Corinthian column pairs, and a ribbed hemispherical dome terminating in an octagonal lantern cupola. Flanking wings comprise continuous three-storey plus attic and rusticated basement Georgian palace-front terraced townhouses (Adam New Town scheme) characterized by rigorous vertical bay alignments, 6-over-6 timber sash-and-case fenestration, rusticated ground-floor masonry, projecting continuous stringcourses, and pitched roofs clad in Scottish slate with heavy ashlar chimneystacks. In the garden foreground stands the 1876 Prince Albert Memorial, featuring an equestrian bronze figure atop a multi-tiered polished granite pedestal with secondary sculptural bronze groupings at the corners.
